iter670 — FIX-A: Trino-Iceberg-default-is-MoR-not-CoW clarification. iter669 Q1 (Iceberg row-level UPDATE) scored 3.75 FLAGGED — the responder's tangential storage-mode note claimed 'CoW default' for Trino 467, which is MATERIALLY WRONG. Trino 467's Iceberg connector performs row-level UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE in MERGE-ON-READ mode by DEFAULT (writes position-delete files + new data files for changed rows), NOT a full copy-on-write file rewrite. Copy-on-write is a Spark-side write-mode option and full CoW in Trino is a roadmap item (trinodb/trino#17272), NOT the Trino 467 default.

=== GREP BEFORE (CoW/MoR-default content audit) ===

Grep across resources/*.md for 'copy-on-write', 'CoW', 'merge-on-read', 'MoR', 'write.update.mode', 'write.delete.mode', 'position delete'. Found ~70 hits across r05/r11/r13/r14/r16/r17/r22/r28. Key verified-false / misleading content for the Trino-execution case:

• **r17:526 (Pattern A UPDATE backfill):** said 'On CoW tables (the Iceberg 1.5.2 default for write.update.mode): Trino rewrites every affected data file with the new column populated.' — FALSE on Trino 467 (Trino's writer is MoR-only regardless of property per #17272).
• **r17:649-650 (operation-table rows):** lumped 'UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE (CoW = Iceberg 1.5.2 default)' with 'Full Parquet data files rewritten' — true only for Spark-executed DML; misleading for Trino-executed DML.
• **r17:653 (Quick fact callout):** stated 'Merge-on-Read is NOT the default; it must be explicitly set in TBLPROPERTIES' — true for the library property but misleading without the Trino-execution caveat.
• **r17:1505 (GDPR 4-step CoW vs MoR section):** said 'Copy-on-Write (CoW) — the Iceberg 1.5.2 default for DELETE, UPDATE, and MERGE. Step 1 already rewrites the affected data files immediately' — true only for Spark-executed DELETE; Trino-executed DELETE writes position-delete files regardless.
• **r17:1735 ('When does this apply?' for rewrite_position_delete_files):** said 'Only if your table is using MoR — i.e., someone explicitly set write.delete.mode = merge-on-read. The Iceberg 1.5.2 default is CoW, which does NOT produce position delete files' — INCOMPLETE; any Trino-executed UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE produces position-delete files regardless of property on this stack.
• **r17:1893 ('For CoW tables ... skip step 2'):** misleading on this stack where Trino is the primary DML engine.
• **r17:2362, r17:2489 (Spark CronJob diagram + comments):** 'MoR TABLES ONLY' / 'SKIP THIS STEP entirely if the table uses CoW' — misleading for the Trino-DML-on-this-stack common case.
• **r17:369 (4-step type-change pattern backfill comment):** 'Trino UPDATE on CoW tables' implication — misleading.
• **r05:3225 ('Merge-on-Read (MoR — the default in most production configs)'):** contradicts r17:653 (which says CoW is the library default); also wrong framing on this stack.
• **r05:3224 ('Copy-on-Write (CoW): DELETE FROM rewrites all affected Parquet data files immediately'):** true only for Spark — Trino DELETE always produces position deletes regardless.
• **r14:407 ('CoW is the default for all three operations'):** true at the library/property level but missing the Trino-execution caveat.
• **r13:2999 ('CRITICAL — Iceberg 1.5.2 default write mode is Copy-on-Write'):** true at the library/property level but didn't carry the Trino-MoR-only caveat into the CDC discussion.
• **r13:5054 ('Iceberg defaults to Copy-on-Write (CoW) for MERGE INTO'):** misleading when read in a dbt-trino-on-Trino-467 context — dbt-trino MERGE is always MoR.
• **r13:5563 ('Copy-on-Write (CoW) — Iceberg 1.5.2 default ... Best for daily/hourly dbt incremental batches ... stick with the CoW default'):** WRONG for dbt-trino — dbt-trino MERGE is always MoR on Trino 467.
• **r11:370 ('every UPDATE, DELETE, or MERGE on a copy-on-write (CoW) table rewrites the affected data files'):** true only for Spark-executed DML.
• **r16:74, r16:143 ('on a format-version 2 table with write.delete.mode = merge-on-read, MERGE/UPDATE/DELETE write position-delete files INSTEAD'):** incomplete — any Trino UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE also produces position-delete files regardless of the property.

=== DOCS-TRUTH VERIFIED (2026-06-08) ===

• **trino.io/docs/467/connector/iceberg.html** (WebFetch): Iceberg connector supports INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE; row-level deletion on v2 tables 'by writing position delete files'. No CoW write mode mentioned in 467 connector docs — only position-delete files for row-level deletes. EXECUTE optimize compacts files but no documented switch for write mode.
• **trinodb/trino#17272** (WebFetch): VERIFIED current — 'Today Iceberg writes only support merge-on-read mode. Copy-on-write mode is a frequent ask...' Issue OPEN; CoW for Iceberg writes NOT implemented in 467; tracked as a roadmap item.
• **trinodb/trino#24086** (WebFetch): VERIFIED — 'Position deletes are local to a partition. OPTIMIZE supports only enforced predicates which select whole partitions. Therefore, we can clean up position deletes in OPTIMIZE when there are no path or file_modified_time predicates.'
• **trinodb/trino#27371** (WebFetch): VERIFIED — issue tracks 'Adding RewritePositionDeleteFiles to trino similar to Spark's RewritePositionDeleteFiles' — feature currently exists in Spark, NOT yet available in Trino 467.
• **Iceberg 1.5.2 TableProperties.java library defaults:** DELETE_MODE_DEFAULT = COPY_ON_WRITE / UPDATE_MODE_DEFAULT = COPY_ON_WRITE / MERGE_MODE_DEFAULT = COPY_ON_WRITE — UNCHANGED (this is the property default for Spark-executed DML; does not govern Trino 467 writer behavior). Confirms the key distinction now made explicit across all edits.
